counterevidence_considered.description: Unlike a definition that binds codes to units, this task explicitly declares k1 and k2 opaque and states that it does not establish whether either code identifies a source item, so the repeated k1 codes cannot be shown from the visible files to be repeated entries of the same unit.

source_refs.quoted_text: Apply the named procedure to the complete staged row sequence. The table stores two disjoint collections of source items measured by columns `a` and `b`. Treat `k1` and `k2` as opaque codes; `tag` is an opaque annotation. This task does not establish whether either code identifies a source item within either collection. The row pairing is a storage convention only; there is no matching, pairing, block, or other relationship between the items represented in that row.

evidence.description: Each k1 code appears exactly twice with different measurement values (e.g., u01 with a=1.0 and a=2.0, through u06 with a=11.0 and a=12.0), so if k1 codes identified source items, each first-collection unit would enter the a-sample twice.
evidence.observed_value: 6 distinct k1 codes over 12 rows, each appearing twice

evidence.description: The workflow enters all 12 a-values into an independent-samples t-test, which treats them as 12 independent observations (df=22.0), so the procedure is row-independent and would be affected if the repeated codes denote repeated units.

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I attempted to resolve the verdict in both directions. Toward 'demonstrated': the doubled k1 codes with distinct a-values strongly resemble repeated measurements of six units entering a row-independent test, but the governing task explicitly withholds the code-to-unit mapping, so asserting the issue would require guessing unstated semantics, which the review protocol forbids. Toward 'no demonstrated issue': the same withheld mapping also prevents me from ruling the issue out, because if u-codes do identify units the report demonstrably double-counts each of six units. The determination is blocked by a fact the visible files deliberately leave open, so neither definitive verdict is supportable.

unresolved_material_questions: Does a repeated k1 code (each of u01–u06 appears on exactly two rows) denote the same first-collection source item, such that its two a-values are repeated entries of one independent unit into the independent-samples t-test?
